data.narrative:
Seneca operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector at Series A stage, having raised $60M to date. The comp universe consists of 8 private peers in this space, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air; no public comparables exist in this narrow vertical, limiting traditional public-market triangulation.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with comparable valuations, peer-median methodology is not reliably applicable. Instead, stage-progression analysis anchors the valuation: using total raised of $60M as a proxy for pre-money valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression to later stages implies a post-money valuation of $120M. This single-method result constrains sensitivity analysis, with a low case at $102M (15% downside buffer) and a high case at $138M (15% upside buffer), yielding a triangulated range of $102M to $138M with a median of $120M.

The primary uncertainty is methodological: reliance on a single approach reflects sparse public data and the difficulty of identifying precisely-comparable private companies in frontier autonomous systems. Material valuation movement would require either: (i) identification of additional transactional comps at adjacent stages with disclosed terms, or (ii) fundamental reassessment of stage-progression multiples specific to frontier-tech capital efficiency and exit outcomes in this sector.
